These functions select and validate the rational coefficients used to
approximate the inverse fractional spatial operator. Let
\(L_h\) be the continuous piecewise linear finite element approximation of
\(L=\kappa^2-\Delta_\Gamma\), and put \(\beta=\alpha/2\). For
\(0<\beta<1\), the scalar function evaluated on normalized eigenvalues is

\[
\mathcal R_{m,\beta}(z)
=F_{m,\beta}
\frac{\prod_{i=1}^{m}(1-\xi_{m,i}z)}
     {\prod_{i=1}^{m+1}(1-\zeta_{m,i}z)}
\approx z^{-\beta},\qquad z>0.
\]

To see the root convention, write
\(q_1(x)=c_m\prod_{i=1}^m(x-\xi_{m,i})\) and
\(q_2(x)=b_{m+1}\prod_{i=1}^{m+1}(x-\zeta_{m,i})\).
Approximating \(x^{\beta-1}\) by \(q_1/q_2\), and then setting
\(x=z^{-1}\), gives

\[
x\frac{q_1(x)}{q_2(x)}=\mathcal R_{m,\beta}(z),\qquad
F_{m,\beta}=c_m/b_{m+1}.
\]

The returned fields use this correspondence:

| Mathematical quantity | List field | Computed CSV kind |
|---|---|---|
| Positive factor \(F_{m,\beta}\) | `factor` | `factor`, index 0 |
| Numerator roots \(\xi_{m,i}\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\) | `pr_roots` | `rc` |
| Denominator roots \(\zeta_{m,i}\), \(i=1,\ldots,m+1\) | `pl_roots` | `rb` |

These are roots in the reciprocal variable \(x\); the poles of
\(\mathcal R(z)\) are \(1/\zeta_{m,i}\). The modal solver uses
\(D\kappa^{2\beta}/\mathcal R_{m,\beta}(\lambda_{j,h}/\kappa^2)\)
as the approximate decay rate. It evaluates the products directly, so this
minimal implementation needs no partial fraction decomposition.

The computed coefficients were generated offline by Cheb--Padé
approximation on \([\delta_m,1]\), where
\(\delta_m=10^{-(5+m)/2}\), for orders 1 through 8 at
\(\beta\in\{0.25,0.45,0.65\}\). The notebooks read the supplied artifact;
they do not run MATLAB. Root validation checks its algebraic structure.
It does not certify a uniform approximation error over every finite element
eigenvalue. A uniform operator estimate would also require coverage of the
normalized spectrum by the generation interval and appropriate approximation
error control.

## `rational_supported_orders()`

Returns the available integer orders: `1:4` for `coefficient_source =
"package"` and `1:8` for `"computed"`. `match.arg()` selects one of these
two sources. This helper describes table availability, not a rule for choosing
\(m\) to meet an error tolerance. The special diagnostic `m = 0` is handled
in `rational_modal_rates()` before any table lookup.

```{r}
rational_supported_orders <- function(coefficient_source = "package") {
  coefficient_source <- match.arg(coefficient_source, c("package", "computed"))
  if (coefficient_source == "package") 1:4 else 1:8
}
```

## `read_computed_fractional_roots()`

Reads `matlab/computed_fractional_roots.csv` relative to the project root
and returns its data frame. Each record has key `(m, beta, kind, index)`
and a numeric `value` representing one entry of \(F\), \(\xi\), or
\(\zeta\) in the product above.

The schema must be exactly `m,beta,kind,index,value`. The reader checks
numeric finite fields, orders in `1:8`, \(0.25\leq\beta<1\), allowed
record kinds, and absence of duplicate keys. These are whole-file checks;
completeness of the selected root set and its mathematical admissibility
are checked subsequently by `my.get.roots()` and
`validate_fractional_roots()`.

```{r}
read_computed_fractional_roots <- function() {
  path <- here::here("matlab", "computed_fractional_roots.csv")
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing computed coefficients: ", path)
  tab <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (!identical(names(tab), c("m", "beta", "kind", "index", "value")) ||
      !all(vapply(tab[c("m", "beta", "index", "value")], is.numeric, logical(1))) ||
      !all(is.finite(as.matrix(tab[c("m", "beta", "index", "value")]))) ||
      !all(tab$m %in% 1:8) || !all(tab$beta >= .25 & tab$beta < 1) ||
      !all(tab$kind %in% c("factor", "rc", "rb")) ||
      anyDuplicated(tab[c("m", "beta", "kind", "index")]))
    stop("Malformed computed coefficient artifact.")
  tab
}
```

## `validate_fractional_roots()`

Checks one coefficient set of order `m` and returns it unchanged on success.
There must be \(m\) numerator roots, \(m+1\) denominator roots, and one
finite positive factor. All roots must be numeric, real, finite, and strictly
negative. After sorting each root family increasingly, the inequalities are

\[
\zeta_1<\xi_1<\zeta_2<\xi_2<\cdots<\zeta_m<\xi_m<\zeta_{m+1}<0.
\]

`denominator[-length(denominator)] < numerator` checks the left inequalities;
`numerator < denominator[-1L]` checks the right ones. Sorting is local to
validation: the original list and root order are returned. For \(z>0\),
negative roots make every factor \(1-\xi_i z\) and \(1-\zeta_i z\)
positive, so a positive \(F\) gives a positive rational inverse and hence
positive modal decay rates. Interlacing is an additional structural check;
it is not a numerical bound on \(|\mathcal R(z)-z^{-\beta}|\).

```{r}
validate_fractional_roots <- function(roots, m) {
  all_roots <- c(roots$pr_roots, roots$pl_roots)
  if (length(roots$pr_roots) != m || length(roots$pl_roots) != m+1L ||
      length(roots$factor) != 1L || !is.finite(roots$factor) || roots$factor <= 0 ||
      !is.numeric(all_roots) || is.complex(all_roots) ||
      any(!is.finite(all_roots)) || any(all_roots >= 0))
    stop("Fractional coefficients need a positive factor and real negative roots.")
  numerator <- sort(roots$pr_roots)
  denominator <- sort(roots$pl_roots)
  if (any(denominator[-length(denominator)] >= numerator) ||
      any(numerator >= denominator[-1L]))
    stop("Fractional coefficient roots do not interlace; this approximation is unsafe.")
  roots
}
```

## `my.get.roots()`

Selects the coefficient set for scalar order `m` and scalar `beta`, returning
the validated list `list(pl_roots, pr_roots, factor)` in the convention above.
The accepted fractional range is \(0.25\leq\beta<1\), or
\(0.5\leq\alpha<2\). The integer case \(\beta=1\) bypasses this function
in the rate evaluator.

With `coefficient_source = "computed"`, rows must have the requested order
and the same beta within floating-point roundoff:

\[
|\beta_{\mathrm{row}}-\beta|
\leq32\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mach}}\max(1,|\beta|).
\]

The nested `values()` helper requires exactly index 0 for the factor,
indices \(1,\ldots,m\) for `rc`, and indices \(1,\ldots,m+1\) for
`rb`, and reorders rows by those indices. An unavailable beta or an
incomplete block raises an error. This branch returns before the
interpolation code: its `interpolation` argument does not interpolate
computed coefficients, and order eight uses its own stored coefficient set.

With `coefficient_source = "package"` (this function's default), the function
loads `m1table` through `m4table` from the `rSPDE` namespace. Each factor or
root column is interpolated independently in beta. For a column \(v\),
linear interpolation between adjacent table entries is

\[
v(\beta)=(1-t)v(\beta_\ell)+t v(\beta_{\ell+1}),\qquad
t=\frac{\beta-\beta_\ell}{\beta_{\ell+1}-\beta_\ell}.
\]

The `"cubic"` option instead uses `splinefun(..., method = "fmm")`.
The nested `interpolate()` helper implements these alternatives. Column
`rc` is used at \(m=1\); higher orders use `rc.1`, ..., `rc.m`, while
denominator columns are `rb.1`, ..., `rb.(m+1)`. Both sources pass through
the same root validation. The convergence wrapper explicitly selects
`"computed"`, overriding this selector's package default.

```{r}
my.get.roots <- function(m,
                         beta, # smoothness parameter, beta = alpha/2
                         interpolation = c("linear", "cubic"),
                         coefficient_source = "package"
                         ) {
  coefficient_source <- match.arg(coefficient_source, c("package", "computed"))
  interpolation <- match.arg(interpolation)
  orders <- rational_supported_orders(coefficient_source)
  if (length(m) != 1L || !is.finite(m) || !(m %in% orders))
    stop("Coefficient source '", coefficient_source, "' supports m = ",
         paste(orders, collapse = ", "), " only.")
  if (length(beta) != 1L || !is.finite(beta) || beta < 0.25 || beta >= 1)
    stop("Fractional evolution tables require 0.25 <= beta < 1; beta = 1 uses the exact solver.")
  if (coefficient_source == "computed") {
    tab <- read_computed_fractional_roots()
    rows <- tab[tab$m == m & abs(tab$beta-beta) <= 32*.Machine$double.eps*max(1, abs(beta)), ]
    if (!nrow(rows)) stop("Computed coefficients are unavailable at beta = ",
      format(beta, digits = 16), ". Available beta: ",
      paste(sort(unique(tab$beta)), collapse = ", "),
      ". Generate and validate new coefficients; beta interpolation is disabled.")
    values <- function(kind, indices) {
      part <- rows[rows$kind == kind, ]
      if (nrow(part) != length(indices) || !setequal(part$index, indices))
        stop("Computed coefficient entries are incomplete for m = ", m, ".")
      part$value[match(indices, part$index)]
    }
    return(validate_fractional_roots(list(factor = values("factor", 0),
      pr_roots = values("rc", seq_len(m)), pl_roots = values("rb", seq_len(m+1L))), m))
  }
  mt <- get(paste0("m", m, "table"), envir = asNamespace("rSPDE"))
  interpolate <- function(column) {
    if (interpolation == "linear") approx(mt$beta, mt[[column]], beta)$y else
      splinefun(mt$beta, mt[[column]], method = "fmm")(beta)
  }
  rb <- rep(0, m + 1)
  rc <- rep(0, m)
  if(m == 1) {
    rc = interpolate("rc")
  } else {
    rc = sapply(1:m, function(i) {
      interpolate(paste0("rc.", i))
    })
  }
  rb = sapply(1:(m+1), function(i) {
    interpolate(paste0("rb.", i))
  })
  factor = interpolate("factor")
  return(validate_fractional_roots(list(pl_roots = rb, # roots \{r_{2j}\}_{j=1}^{m+1}
              pr_roots = rc, # roots \{r_{1i}\}_{i=1}^m
              factor = factor # this is c_m/b_{m+1}
              ), m))
}
```
